messages:
Ava (Partnerships): Hi team — Lena from CoreSilicon and I spoke about doing a joint benchmark for our inference runtime on their QX-900 GPU. Goal: a public performance/efficiency report (perf/W) and a reproducible benchmark we can share in the marketplace listing. Thoughts? :sparkles:
Lena (HW Partner): excited! we can provide early silicon and nvml telemetry. prefer we test both FP16 and 4-bit quantized kernels. we have internal kernel patches that improve streaming KV cache perf.
Diego (Platform): +1. we'll want to validate across our hosted cluster and a dedicated reserved pool to show production numbers. can we define exact workloads and measurement method up front?
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): Suggested workloads: 1) long-context decode (2k tokens) single-stream p99 latency, 2) medium-batch throughput (batch=16, seq=512) tokens/sec, 3) perf/W microbench (steady-state 5-min run while sampling NVML). Also quantify model variants: base fp16, int8/4-bit quantized. Warmup & KV cache priming required.
Priya (Solutions): We should include a customer-style scenario: chat + tool-calling mix, and an embeddings rerank pass. marketing will like a simple P95 latency + $/token and perf/W headline.
Ava (Partnerships): Good list. For public report we'll need: reproducible harness (docker + commit hash), raw telemetry, and a short artifacts repo with scripts. Can Redwood host the runner image in registry?
Diego (Platform): Yes. we'll prepare image: redwood/bench-runner:partner-qx900-<date>. We'll need a config schema for runs. propose using: `bench_config.yaml` with fields: model, seq_len, batch, quant, kernel_flags, warmup_steps, run_time_s, nvml_poll_interval.
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): Example bench_config snippet I propose:
```yaml
model: redwood-xl-7b
seq_len: 2048
batch: 1
quant: int4
kernel_flags: enable_streaming_kv: true
warmup_steps: 200
run_time_s: 300
nvml_poll_interval_ms: 500
```
Lena (HW Partner): we'll supply a kernel-optimized container too. need to coordinate CUDA/cutlass/cuBLAS versions. Our preferred stack: CUDA 12.2, cutlass 2.6 patches, driver 555.xx. can Redwood validate those exact versions?
Diego (Platform): yes, we can pin image and driver. but for hosted results we must ensure driver parity with Dedicated testbed. will schedule a maintenance window to reprovision nodes with 555.xx.
Priya (Solutions): timeline ask: marketing needs draft report in 5 weeks for QBR. engineering needs at least 2 weeks for integration and 1 week of validation. is 5 weeks realistic?
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): workable if we start this week. plan: week1 integration (images + configs), week2 kernel tune + smoke runs, week3 full runs and perf/W collection, week4 analysis & writeup, week5 review + signoff.
Ava (Partnerships): Owners: Partnerships = Ava (coord & legal), HW partner = Lena (silicon + kernel patches), Platform = Diego (images + infra), Runtime = Sanjay (bench harness + metrics). Priya will lead report narrative.
Lena (HW Partner): we'll publish kernel diffs in a partner-only branch and provide scripts to apply patches. for public release we can provide a no-patch baseline and a patched result, clearly annotated.
Diego (Platform): one asks: how do we compute perf/W? do we use average power across the 5-min steady-state window, or peak power? I'd recommend average power after warmup. also track energy per token.
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): agree: metric definitions: throughput_tokens_per_s (steady median over window), avg_power_watts (nvml average), energy_per_token = avg_power_watts / throughput_tokens_per_s. report p95/p99 latencies for single-stream tests.
Priya (Solutions): legal/PR check: Ava, can you confirm whether we can use partner logos in the marketplace entry and co-branded blog? also need to confirm embargo dates.
Ava (Partnerships): I'll loop in legal today. initial ask: no embargo, but request 48h notice before publish. We'll include co-branding guidelines and the logos Lena will provide.
Redwood CI Bot: deploy scheduled: reprovision-dedicated-pool -> starts at 1750005400, ETA ~3h.
Diego (Platform): I'll schedule the reprovision for tomorrow and upload the bench image to our registry. will create a README in the artifacts repo with exact commands to reproduce.
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): small gotcha: quantized int4 kernels can change tokenization perf slightly; include identical tokenization pipeline and seed for sampling to keep outputs comparable. will add checksum script to the harness.
Lena (HW Partner): noted. we'll also provide a power cap profile to test perf/W tradeoffs (e.g., 250W vs 300W). that could be a nice data point for customers.
Priya (Solutions): marketing ask: provide 3 slides-worth of highlights and 1 tweet-ready sentence. I'll draft after raw numbers.
Ava (Partnerships): OK — action items: 1) Diego: upload `redwood/bench-runner:partner-qx900-2025-09-01`, create bench_config template (due in 3 days). 2) Sanjay: implement harness + checksum + nvml sampler (due in 6 days). 3) Lena: provide kernel patch branch + driver matrix + power profiles (due in 4 days). 4) Priya: draft report skeleton and PR checklist (due in 7 days). I'll loop legal for co-branding.
Lena (HW Partner): sounds good. we'll also set up a shared s3 bucket for telemetry dumps.
Diego (Platform): creating GH issue and infra tickets now. assigning owners.
Ava (Partnerships): thanks all — will follow up with calendar invites for a kick-off tomorrow. :calendar:
Priya (Solutions): thanks — excited to get numbers.
Sanjay (Eng - Runtime): on it.
Redwood CI Bot: task created: #bench-qx900-1750001234 (CI job link: https://ci.redwood.example/bench-qx900-1750001234)
